expression: This means that Calibration Parameters can be defined bullet individually for a SwComponentPrototype in the SwcInternalBehavior of a SwComponentType via an aggregation of an ParameterDataPrototype in the role of perInstanceParameter (similar to PerInstanceMemory) (see chapter 2.2.3.3) bullet sharing between all SwComponentPrototypes of the same SwComponentType in its SwcInternalBehavior via an aggregation of an ParameterDataPrototype in the role of sharedParameter or constantMemory (see chapter 2.2.3.2) bullet for several SwComponentPrototypes (using the port-/interface-concept with ParameterInterfaces) (see chapter 2.2.3.1).
title: Ways to define a calibration parameter

expression: Every SwComponentType requiring access to shared calibration parameters will have an RPortPrototype typed by a ParameterInterface. The definition of this shared calibration access in the context of a CompositionSwComponentType will be defined by creating a SwConnector between the relevant SwComponentPrototypes.
title: SwComponentType requiring access to shared calibration parameters needs RPortPrototype typed by a ParameterInterface

expression: Note that a ParameterInterface is not restricted to parameters which can actually can be calibrated. It can be used whenever there shall be no write access to the data during normal operation of the software, i.e. only constant data are visible over the interface.
title: ParameterInterface is not restricted to parameters which can actually can be calibrated

expression: Access to shared calibration parameters can be provided and required even over CompositionSwComponentTypes using DelegationSwConnectors and AssemblySwConnectors. This means that each access to calibration parameters between SwComponentPrototypes is explicitly visible. If a SwConnector spans after the mapping of SwComponentPrototypes over two different ECUs the system generation process has to ensure the proper allocation of the ParameterDataPrototype (see Figure 2.2) while the calibration system has to cope with setting the parameter synchronously on the affected ECUs.
title: Delegation of PortPrototypes typed by a ParameterInterface

expression: Additionally, it is possible to describe the implementation of shared characteristic values via a ParameterDataPrototype which is attached to an SwcInternalBehavior in the role constantMemory. In contrast to the ParameterDataPrototype in sharedParameter role this kind of memory is not instantiated by the RTE. This supports more efficient implementations (especially for software components provided as object code) by avoidance of the additional indirection caused by the RTE’s component data structure.
title: ParameterDataPrototype aggregated in the role constantMemory

expression: To provide instance individual calibration parameters a ParameterDataPrototype is owned by a SwcInternalBehavior in perInstanceParameter role. When the SwcInternalBehavior is attached to an AtomicSwComponentType, the actual calibration values are specific for each SwComponentPrototype.
title: ParameterDataPrototype aggregated in the role perInstanceParameter

expression: The Variant Handling support in the in Software Component Template is mainly driven by the purpose to describe a variable system on Virtual Functional Bus[3] level by varying bullet the existence of SwComponentPrototypes bullet the existence of SwConnectors bullet the existence of Chapters of SwComponentDocumentation bullet the existence of PortPrototypes
title: Support for Variant Handling in the in Software Component Template

expression: This supports adjusting the number and kind of software-component instances as well as their interconnection in a particular system variant.
title: Purpose of variant handling

expression: The first three cases are supporting PostBuild binding. For the existence of PortPrototypes only preCompileTime is supported as latest Binding Time.
title: Applicable binding times for model elements in the scope of the Software Component Template
enum: Chapters of SwComponentDocumentation: PostBuild binding; Existence of PortPrototypes: preCompileTime latestBindingTime

expression: A SwConnector which exists depending on a PostBuild condition has an impact on the behavior of API function calls that apply on a PortPrototype to which the SwConnector is attached. If the SwConnector does not exist the behavior of the RTE API functions need to take this into account. This means that the RTE implementation of this PortPrototype resembles the behavior of an unconnected PortPrototype.
title: SwConnector exists depending on a PostBuild condition

expression: If SwConnectors do not exist the corresponding API functions are still part of the software-component’s implementation. It is not possible to remove the API functions in a PostBuild step. Therefore the latest reasonable Binding Time for the conditional existence of a PortPrototype is preCompileTime.
title: API functions of not existing SwConnector are still part of the software-component’s implementation

expression: In addition to variation of the VFB-related model elements, the description of variant software-component implementations is supported. Please note that this requires a broad support of variability in the Internal Behavior. The identified main use case are bullet the existence of RunnableEntitys bullet the existence of RTEEvents bullet the existence of VariableDataPrototypes in the roles implicitInterRunnableVariable and explicitInterRunnableVariable bullet the existence of ParameterDataPrototypes in the roles perInstanceParameter, sharedParameter, and constantMemory
title: Variation on the behavior level
condition_expression: in addition to variation of the vfb-related model elements, the description of variant software-component implementations is supported. please note that this requires a broad support of variability in the internal behavior. the identified main use case are bullet the existence of runnableentitys bullet the existence of rteevents bullet the existence of variabledataprototypes in the roles implicitinterrunnablevariable and explicitinterrunnablevariable bullet the existence of parameterdataprototypes in the roles perinstanceparameter, sharedparameter, and constantmemory

expression: For the same reason that applies on the existence of PortPrototype the latest Binding Time of these kinds of variability (existence of RunnableEntitys, RTEEvents, VariableDataPrototypes in roles implicitInterRunnableVariable/explicitInterRunnableVariable, ParameterDataPrototypes in roles perInstanceParameter/sharedParameter/constantMemory) is preCompileTime.
title: Binding Time for Behavioral Element Variability

expression: There are four types of locations in the meta-model which may exhibit variability: bullet Aggregations bullet Associations bullet Attribute Values bullet Classes providing property sets
title: Four types of locations in the meta-model which may exhibit variability

expression: It shall be possible to attach ComSpecs to PortPrototypes owned by CompositionSwComponentTypes.
title: ComSpecs defined by CompositionSwComponentTypes

expression: The RTE Generator shall take the attributes of the RPortComSpec or PPortComSpec of the PortPrototypes owned by AtomicSwComponentTypes or ParameterSwComponentType and ignore the attributes of the RPortComSpec or PPortComSpec attached to PortPrototypes owed by CompositionSwComponentType.
title: Consideration of RPortComSpec or PPortComSpec depending on the ownership

expression: It shall be possible to define mappings of ApplicationDataTypes used in a PortInterface to their corresponding ImplementationDataTypes for a CompositionSwComponentType. For this purpose the CompositionSwComponentType owns a DataTypeMappingSet in the role dataTypeMapping and a ConstantSpecificationMappingSet in the role constantValueMapping.
title: DataType and ConstantValue Mapping Capability for CompositionSwComponentType

expression: The solution to the use cases (requiring combined read/write access to the same data) is the ability to define a PortPrototype (PRPortPrototype) that can read and write the same piece of data.
title: PRPortPrototype Read/Write Capability

expression: The identification of different configuration options for Pretended Networking shall be encoded into the definition of dedicated ModeDeclarations inside a ModeDeclarationGroup.
title: Configuration option is encoded into ModeDeclaration

expression: A SwComponentType that needs to be able to request a change in the operating mode of Pretended Networking shall provide a PPortPrototype typed by a SenderReceiverInterface (see [TPS_SWCT_01086]) for requesting a change (towards the BswM [15]) of the Pretended Networking mode. It is out of the scope of this document to define the particular properties of the applicable SenderReceiverInterface. The details of this specific SenderReceiverInterface can be found in the specification of the BswM [15].
title: Request change of Pretended Networking mode

expression: A SwComponentType that needs to be able to react on a change in the operating mode of Pretended Networking shall provide an RPortPrototype typed by a ModeSwitchInterface (see [TPS_SWCT_01087]) for reacting on a change (initiated by the BswM [15]) of the Pretended Networking mode. It is out of the scope of this document to define the particular properties of the applicable ModeSwitchInterface. The details of this specific ModeSwitchInterface can be found in the specification of the BswM [15].
title: React on the change of Pretended Networking mode

expression: If a Variable-Size Array Data Type is modeled on the level of ApplicationDataType it is necessary to also provide a companion ImplementationDataType as well as a DataTypeMap that refers to both the ApplicationDataType and the ImplementationDataType.
title: Companion ImplementationDataType and DataTypeMap for ApplicationDataType VSADT

expression: It is possible to define a Variable-Size Array Data Type with only an ImplementationDataType.
title: Possibility of VSADT with only ImplementationDataType

expression: The number of valid elements and the Size Indicator have to be kept consistent by the application.
title: Application Responsibility for Size Indicator Consistency

expression: it should be possible to re-use existing artifacts to create further model elements instead of being forced to create every single modeling detail from scratch.
title: Support for re-usability of artifacts

expression: software-components shall not directly call the operating system or the communication hardware.
title: Software components independence from OS and hardware

expression: AtomicSwComponentTypes (and also the more general SwComponentTypes may only interact by means of their PortPrototypes). Hidden communication dependencies that are not expressed by means of PortPrototypes are strictly forbidden.
title: SwComponentTypes may only interact by means of their PortPrototypes

expression: Please note that PortPrototypes actually need an additional model artifact, the PortInterface, for fully describing the details of the PortPro totype. The concept of the PortInterface as another means for establishing a high degree of re-usability is described in chapter 3.4.
title: PortPrototypes need an additional model artifact, the PortInterface

expression: A PRPortPrototype is never considered unconnected, even if there are no SwConnectors actually referring to it.
title: A PRPortPrototype is never considered unconnected

expression: Two SwComponentPrototypes are eventually connected by hooking up a PPortPrototype or PRPortPrototype of one SwComponentPrototype to a compatible RPortPrototype or PRPortPrototype of the other SwComponentPrototypes. Please find more information concerning the definition of “compatibility” in section 6.
title: Connecting two PortPrototypes

expression: PortPrototypes can be logically grouped into PortGroups. This mechanism is used for implementing mode management features and further explained in chapter 4.6.
title: PortGroup

expression: As mentioned before, the term AtomicSwComponentType is a specific form of the general concept of the SwComponentType. The added value of an AtomicSwComponentType is that it can aggregate an InternalBehavior (see chapter 7).
title: Added value of an AtomicSwComponentType

expression: The aggregation of SwcInternalBehavior is stereotyped (cid:28)atpSplitable(cid:29) to allow for adding the SwcInternalBehavior in a later process step. In other words, it is possible to completely develop the VFB view of a software-component and later add more details like InternalBehavior.
title: Adding the SwcInternalBehavior in a later process step

expression: The ParameterSwComponentType is a specialization of SwComponentType that can - in contrast to AtomicSwComponentType - not aggregate SwcInternalBehavior.
title: ParameterSwComponentType cannot aggregate SwcInternalBehavior

expression: A ParameterSwComponentType shall never aggregate a SwcInternalBehavior and also owns exclusively PPortPrototypes of type ParameterInterface.
title: ParameterSwComponentType

expression: a ParameterSwComponentType shall have the ability to aggregate InstantiationDataDefProps.
title: ParameterSwComponentType ability to aggregate InstantiationDataDefProps

expression: To mitigate this potential hazard it is possible to provide the AtomicSwComponentType along with an accompanying symbolic name that can be used for resolving the name clash. The symbolic name is provided by means of the attribute symbol of the meta-class Sym bolProps owned by AtomicSwComponentType in the role symbolProps (for more information, please refer to Figure 3.6).
title: Symbolic name of a software-component

expression: In particular, the RTE generator shall take over the value of the attribute symbol of the symbolProps owned by a given AtomicSwComponentType.If and only if symbolProps is not defined the RTE generator shall take the shortName of the AtomicSwComponentType. For the generation of symbols for RunnableEntitys [TPS_SWCT_01001] shall be observed.
title: Usage of attribute symbol of the symbolProps

expression: If and only if the attribute symbol of a symbolProps owned by an AtomicSwComponentType exists, its value shall also be taken for prefixing the symbols generated for the RunnableEntitys owned by the AtomicSwComponentType.
title: Prefix symbols generated for the RunnableEntity

expression: Of course, there is a residual risk that even in the presence of SymbolProps name clashes may occur. Therefore, the definition of naming conventions may facilitate the avoidance of name clashes to the further degree. However, these naming conventions can (with the support of the meta-model, e.g. by utilizing SymbolProps or shortNamePattern) still only be defined on the model level.
title: Naming conventions may support the effectiveness of SymbolProps

expression: Since a CompositionSwComponentType is also a SwComponentType, it again may be aggregated in further CompositionSwComponentTypes.
title: Nested definition of CompositionSwComponentTypes

expression: the definition of CompositionSwComponentTypes has no effect on how software-components interact with the Virtual Functional Bus (VFB). CompositionSwComponentTypes do not add any new functionality to what is already provided by the software-components they aggregate.
title: CompositionSwComponentTypes effect on VFB and functionality

expression: As the main consequence, CompositionSwComponentTypes do not have any binary footprint in the ECU software.
title: CompositionSwComponentTypes do not have any binary footprint

expression: In terms of the AUTOSAR meta-model, a composition of softwarecomponents realized by the meta-class CompositionSwComponentType aggregates SwComponentPrototypes which in turn are typed by a SwComponentType.
title: CompositionSwComponentType aggregates SwComponentPrototypes

expression: In general, arbitrary numbers of SwComponentPrototypes that refer to specific SwComponentTypes can be created.
title: arbitrary numbers of SwComponentPrototypes can be created

expression: Note that being a SwComponentType, a CompositionSwComponentType also exposes PortPrototypes to the out side world. However,the PortPrototypes are only delegated and do not play the same role as PortPrototypes attached to AtomicSwComponentTypes.
title: Delegation ports

expression: Being a PortPro totype attached to a CompositionSwComponentType has the following implications: bullet The delegation has to follow the rules defined in chapter 6. bullet By creating PortPrototypes on the surface of a specific CompositionSwComponentType it is explicitly decided whether or not the contents of an “inner” port contained in the CompositionSwComponentType is exposed to the outside world.
title: Implications of being a delegation port

expression: a top-level composition might have (unconnected) PortPrototypes in order to allow for reuse as part of another system.
title: Top-level composition unconnected ports for reuse

expression: The recursive definition of a CompositionSwComponentType that eventually contains a SwComponentPrototype typed by the same CompositionSwComponentType shall not be feasible.
title: Recursive definition of CompositionSwComponentType

expression: Note that CompositionSwComponentType also aggregates the abstract meta-class SwConnector for connecting the SwComponentPrototypes contained among each other(see Figure 3.8).
title: SwConnector

expression: A DelegationSwConnector can only connect PortPrototypes of the same kind, i.e. PPortPrototype to PPortPrototype and RPortPrototype to RPortPrototype.
title: DelegationSwConnector can only connect PortPrototypes of the same kind

expression: In the case that an outer PortPrototype is referenced by multiple DelegationSwConnectors the semantic is the multiplication of the AssemblySwConnectors referencing the outer PortPrototypes.
title: Outer PortPrototype is referenced by multiple DelegationSwConnectors

expression: Each pair of PortPrototypes can only be connected by one and only one SwConnector.
title: SwConnector between two specific PortPrototypes

expression: [constr_1086] applies also in the case that two PRPortPrototypes are connected with each other. In particular, the roles bullet AssemblySwConnector.requester bullet AssemblySwConnector.provider bullet PassThroughSwConnector.providedOuterPort bullet PassThroughSwConnector.requiredOuterPort do not establish a direction in this case.
title: Existence of SwConnector between two PRPortPrototypes

expression: An AssemblySwConnector can only connect PortPrototypes of SwComponentPrototypes that are owned by the same CompositionSwComponentType
title: AssemblySwConnector inside CompositionSwComponentType

expression: For the implementation of the attachment of a DelegationSwConnector to an inner PRPortPrototype the meta-class PPortInCompositionInstanceRef shall be used.
title: PPortInCompositionInstanceRef shall be used for attaching DelegationSwConnector to an inner PRPortPrototype

expression: A PassThroughSwConnector is not allowed if the required outer PortPrototype is directly or indirectly connected to the provided outer PortPrototype without the placement of a SwComponentPrototype typed by an AtomicSwComponentType in the chain of SwConnectors.
title: Creation of a loop involving a PassThroughSwConnector is not allowed

expression: It is possible to specify instantiation specific properties of an RTEEvent by applying InstantiationRTEEventProps in the role instantiationRteEventProps.This allows to use the same ApplicationSwComponentType in different timing scenarios. Even if the scheduling is an issue of the SwcInternalBehavior, the instancespecific definition of timing needs to be specified on the level of a CompositionSwComponentType.
title: Instantiation-specific RTEEvents

expression: An InstantiationTimingEventProps shall only reference TimingEvent in the role refinedEvent. A reference to other kinds of RTEEvents is not supported.
title: InstantiationTimingEventProps shall only reference TimingEvent

expression: It shall not be possible to connect PortPrototypes typed by PortInterfaces of different kinds. Subclasses of DataInterface make an exception from this rule and can be used for creating connections to each other.
title: Connect kinds of PortInterfaces

expression: A PPortPrototype typed by a ParameterInterface can only be owned by a ParameterSwComponentType.
title: Applicability of ParameterInterface

expression: In case of inconsistencies between the value of serviceKind and the actual implementation of the PortInterface the implementation of the PortInterface wins over the value of attribute PortInterface.serviceKind (which, for the intended purpose shall be considered an annotation rather than a semantically binding information).
title: Inconsistencies regarding the value of serviceKind and the actual implementation of the PortInterface

expression: if the attribute serviceKind is not defined in the context of a specific PortInterface the default value anyStandardized shall be assumed.
title: Default value if serviceKind is not defined

expression: CompositionSwComponentTypes shall not own PortPrototypes typed by PortInterfaces where the attribute isService is set to true.
title: PortInterfaces used in the context of CompositionSwComponentTypes cannot refer to AUTOSAR services

expression: SwcServiceDependencys can also be used for vendor-specific services.In this case the SwcServiceDependency shall not contain any of the standardized ServiceNeeds.
title: Usage of SwcServiceDependencys for vendor-specific services

expression: A DelegationSwConnector can only connect a PortPrototype of a SwComponentPrototype that is owned by the same CompositionSwComponentType that also owns the connected delegationPortPrototype.
title: DelegationSwConnector inside CompositionSwComponentType

expression: For any element in an unconnected RPortPrototype typed by a DataInterface there shall be a requiredComSpec that defines an initValue.
title: Unconnected RPortPrototype typed by a DataInterface

expression: PortInterfaces are limited to the description of the static structure of the exchanged information; the dynamic attributes (please refer to chapter 4.5) relevant for communication are attached to PortPrototypes.
title: PortInterface describes the static structure of information interchange

expression: The supported value encodings for the usage within a Port Interface are: bullet 2C: Two’s complement bullet IEEE754: floating point numbers bullet ISO-8859-1: ASCII-Strings bullet ISO-8859-2: ASCII-Strings bullet WINDOWS-1252: ASCII-Strings bullet UTF-8: UCS Transformation Format 8 bullet UTF-16: Character encoding for Unicode code points based on 16 bit code units [16] bullet UCS-2: Universal Character Set 2 bullet NONE: Unsigned Integer bullet BOOLEAN: This represents an integer to be interpreted as boolean.
title: Supported value encodings for SwBaseType in the context of PortInterfaces

expression: [constr_1045] applies only if the value of the attribute isService is set to false.
title: Applicability of [constr_1045]

expression: A DataPrototype defined in the context of a PortInterface used by an ApplicationSwComponentType or SensorActuatorSwComponentType that is (after potential indirections via TYPE_REFERENCE are resolved) either typed by or mapped to an ImplementationDataType of category DATA_REFERENCE shall only be used if either the provider or the requester of the information represents a ServiceSwComponentType, a ComplexDeviceDriverSwComponentType, a ParameterSwComponentType, or an NvBlockSwComponentType, or the EcuAbstractionSwComponentType.
title: PortInterfaces and category DATA_REFERENCE

expression: SenderReceiverInterfaces allow for the specification of the typically asynchronous communication pattern where a sender provides data that is required by one or more receivers. While the actual communication takes place via the respective PortPrototypes, a SenderReceiverInterface allows for formally describing what kind of information is sent and received.
title: SenderReceiverInterface

expression: If no invalidationPolicy points to a dataElement in a SenderReceiverInterface, this is considered to yield the identical result as if the handleInvalid attribute was set to dontInvalidate.
title: Default behavior of invalidationPolicy for SenderReceiverInterface

expression: HandleInvalidEnum defines strategies for handling invalid values. These strategies include: Invalidation is switched off. Replace a received invalidValue where the replacement value is sourced from the externalReplacement. The application software is supposed to handle signal invalidation on RTE API level either by DataReceiveErrorEvent or check of error code on read access. Replace a received invalidValue where the replacement value is specified by the initValue.
title: Definition of HandleInvalidEnum literals

expression: An invalidationPolicy specifies whether the sending component can actively invalidate a particular dataElement and which strategy of handling the reception of invalidValue on the receiver side shall be implemented.
title: invalidationPolicy

expression: A SenderReceiverInterface provides a name space for the definition of VariableDataPrototypes. This is indicated by its inheritance relation (ultimately from Identifiable via DataPrototype).
title: SenderReceiverInterface as namespace for VariableDataPrototypes

expression: The swImplPolicy (see section 5.4) indicates the way how a VariableDataPrototype shall be processed at the receiver's side. If set to queued the semantics is that the corresponding VariableDataPrototype needs to be added to a queue (or in other words: a FIFO data structure) from which it is later consumed by the actual receiver software-component.
title: swImplPolicy

expression: The swImplPolicy shall not be set to queued for any dataElement owned by a PRPortPrototype.
title: Queued communication is not applicable for dataElements owned by PRPortPrototype

expression: If swImplPolicy is set to any other valid value of SwImplPolicyEnum then last is best semantics applies.
title: last-is-best semantics for sender-receiver communication
if_condition: swImplPolicy is set to any other valid value of SwImplPolicyEnum
then_action: last is best semantics applies.

expression: PortPrototypes typed by a SenderReceiverInterface may be connected to establish a 1:n (i.e. one sender, multiple receivers) communication relationship. It is also possible to establish a n:1 (i.e. many senders, one receiver) communication pattern.
title: Communication patterns for sender-receiver communication

expression: For sender/receiver communication, it is not allowed to create a communication scenario where n sender are connected to m receivers where m and n are both greater than 1.
title: Communication scenarios for sender/receiver communication

expression: For the modeling of AssemblySwConnectors between PortPrototypes typed by a SenderReceiverInterface or NvDataInterface, only the connections documented in Table 4.4 are supported by AUTOSAR.
title: Supported connections by AssemblySwConnector for PortPrototypes typed by a SenderReceiverInterface or NvDataInterface

RPort-RPort:No, RPort-PPort:Yes, RPort-PRPort:Yes. PPort-RPort:Yes, PPort-PPort:No, PPort-PRPort:Yes. PRPort-RPort:Yes, PRPort-PPort:Yes, PRPort-PRPort:No.
title: Supported AssemblySwConnector connections (SenderReceiver/NvDataInterface)

expression: For the modeling of DelegationSwConnectors between PortPrototypes typed by a SenderReceiverInterface or NvDataInterface, only the connections documented in Table 4.5 are supported by AUTOSAR.
title: Supported connections by DelegationSwConnector for PortPrototypes typed by a SenderReceiverInterface or NvDataInterface

expression: Specifies allowed connections for DelegationSwConnector between innerPort and outerPort (RPort, PPort, PRPort subtypes) typed by SenderReceiverInterface or NvDataInterface. InnerRPort-OuterRPort:Yes, InnerRPort-OuterPPort:No, InnerRPort-OuterPRPort:Yes. InnerPPort-OuterRPort:No, InnerPPort-OuterPPort:Yes, InnerPPort-OuterPRPort:Yes. InnerPRPort-OuterRPort:Yes, InnerPRPort-OuterPPort:Yes, InnerPRPort-OuterPRPort:Yes.
title: Supported DelegationSwConnector connections (SenderReceiver/NvDataInterface)

expression: A client shall not be connected to multiple servers such that an operation call would be handled by more than one server.
title: Client shall not be connected to multiple servers

expression: As depicted in Figure 4.2, a ClientServerInterface is composed of ClientServerOperations, i.e. a ClientServerOperation cannot be reused in the context of a different ClientServerInterface
title: ClientServerInterface

expression: A ClientServerOperation consists of 0..* ArgumentDataPrototypes. The latter may be bullet passed to the operation (i.e. the direction is "in") bullet passed to and returned from the operation (i.e. the direction is "inout") bullet returned from the operation (i.e. the direction is "out") The aggregation represents a variation point.
title: ClientServerOperation

expression: To cover these cases, ArgumentDataPrototype defines an attribute direction, possible values are in (pass to operation), out (return from operation), and inout (pass to and return from operation).
title: Direction of ArgumentDataPrototypes

expression: It is not possible to pass a reference to a ClientServerOperation as an ArgumentDataPrototype in another ClientServerOperation.
title: ClientServerOperation cannot be passed as a reference

expression: When the client invokes an operation, it needs to provide a value for each ArgumentDataPrototype that is of direction in or inout.
title: Client needs to provide ArgumentDataPrototypes

expression: The value passed to an ArgumentDataPrototype of direction in or inout needs to be of the corresponding Datatype.
title: Pass correct data type

expression: In the case of synchronous operation call, the client expects to receive a response to the invocation of the operation. As part of the response, it receives a value (of the correct AutosarDataType) for each ArgumentDataPrototype that is of direction out or inout.
title: Synchronous call of ClientServerOperation

expression: It is not possible to define default values for ArgumentDataPrototypes defined in the context of a ClientServerOperation. Default values might lead to complicated mappings to programming languages.
title: No default values for ArgumentDataPrototypes

expression: The option useArrayBaseType is intended to implement "Server Runnables" which are able to handle array typed arguments of different length. In this case the software component does have several Server Ports. At least one argument of the ClientServerOperations is typed by AutosarDataTypes of category ARRAY but the length of the arrays defined by ApplicationArrayElement.maxNumberOfElements respectively arraySize might be different for the individual Server Ports. All ClientServerOperations in the PortPrototypes are triggering the same RunnableEntity with OperationInvokedEvents. If the serverArgumentImplPolicy is set to useArrayBaseType the RTE Generator does not require the compatibility of ClientServerOperations for such ArgumentDataPrototypes and uses the baseType of the array as the argument's data type instead of the array data type with a particular length. The option useVoid is available to implement Server RunnableEntitys which are able to handle arbitrary typed arguments of different length - typically of category STRUCTURE. The design of the software component implementing the server is similar as explained for useArrayBaseType. If the serverArgumentImplPolicy is set to useVoid the RTE Generator does not require the compatibility of ClientServerOperations for such ArgumentDataPrototypes and uses void as the argument data type.
title: serverArgumentImplPolicy

expression: The value of the attribute ArgumentDataPrototype.serverArgumentImplPolicy shall only be set to useArrayBaseType for an ArgumentDataPrototype that is (after all TYPE_REFERENCEs are resolved) either an ImplementationDataType of category ARRAY or an ApplicationDataType mapped to (after all TYPE_REFERENCEs are resolved) an ImplementationDataType of category ARRAY.
title: Applicability of serverArgumentImplPolicy set to useArrayBaseType

expression: The value of the attribute ArgumentDataPrototype.serverArgumentImplPolicy shall not be set to useVoid for an ArgumentDataPrototype of direction in that is typed by an AutosarDataType that boils down to a primitive C data type (see [TPS_SWCT_01565]).
title: serverArgumentImplPolicy and ArgumentDataPrototype typed by primitive data types

expression: For the modeling of AssemblySwConnectors between PortPrototypes typed by a ClientServerInterface, ModeSwitchInterface, or TriggerInterface, only the connections documented in Table 4.11 are supported by AUTOSAR.
title: Supported connections by AssemblySwConnector for Port Prototypes typed by a ClientServerInterface, ModeSwitchInterface, or TriggerInterface

expression: For the modeling of DelegationSwConnectors between PortPrototypes typed by a ClientServerInterface, ModeSwitchInterface, or TriggerInterface, only the connections documented in Table 4.12 are supported by AUTOSAR.
title: Supported connections by DelegationSwConnector for Port Prototypes typed by a ClientServerInterface, ModeSwitchInterface, or TriggerInterface

expression: As the fixed set of infrastructure errors is defined as an implicit part of the VFB, a developer of an AUTOSAR system does not need to explicitly describe these. It is assumed that these might occur at run-time and application developers should take measures to handle them.
title: AUTOSAR system does not need to explicitly describe infrastructure errors

expression: As of now, AUTOSAR supports (as depicted by Figure 4.4) ApplicationErrors only for ClientServerInterfaces.
title: AUTOSAR supports ApplicationErrors only for ClientServerInterfaces

expression: The value of ApplicationError.errorCode shall not exceed the closed interval 1 .. 63. The following exception applies: only in case possibleError is supposed to represent E_OK the value 0 shall be be allowed.
title: Value of ApplicationError.errorCode

expression: A possibleError referenced by a ClientServerOperation shall be owned by the ClientServerInterface that also owns the ClientServerOperation.
title: Reference to ApplicationError

expression: The underlying semantics of an external trigger event communication is that a trigger source may initiate the execution of RunnableEntitys in the connected trigger sinks. Typically (but not necessarily) these RunnableEntitys are executed in a sequential order.
title: Semantics of an external trigger event communication

expression: The TriggerInterface defines a set of Trigger to be communicated between software-components. The Trigger represents a special kind of events at which occurrence the trigger sinks shall react in a particular manner.
title: TriggerInterface

expression: A Trigger can optionally define a period for periodic triggering. It is expressed via the meta-class MultidimensionalTime in terms of time or angle. Note that the main use case for this is to specify the properties if the trigger is coming from the Basic Software e.g. from a Complex Driver, it is not used as an input for the RTE generator.
title: Period for periodic triggering

expression: An RPortPrototype typed by a TriggerInterface shall not be referenced by more than one SwConnectors that are in turn referencing PPortPrototypes typed by TriggerInterfaces that contain Triggers with the same shortName.
title: Trigger sink and trigger source

expression: It may happen that at least tentatively a Trigger source fires Triggers faster than they can be processed on the side of the Trigger sink. To support this use case it is possible to process trigger event communication in a queued manner. In this case the Triggers are added to a queue from where the foremost trigger is dequeued and processed when the processing of the current Trigger is done. Please note that the queue size is not subject to definition in the scope of this document. The actual queue size is defined during the process of RTE configuration. The specification of whether or not a Trigger is subject to queued processing is controlled by the attribute Trigger.swImplPolicy.
title: Queued processing of Triggers

expression: The only allowed values for the attribute Trigger.swImplPolicy are either STANDARD (in which case the Trigger processing does not use a queue) or QUEUED (in which case the processing of Triggers positively uses a queue).
title: Allowed values for Trigger.swImplPolicy

expression: For communicating a mode switch (i.e. the first use case), the Software-Component Template describes the concept of the communication of ModeDeclarationGroupPrototypes similar to the communication of VariableDataPrototypes but is uses a special type of PortInterface: the collections of ModeDeclarations that are required or provided by a SwComponentType are defined (as depicted in Figure 4.6) by means of ModeSwitchInterfaces used to type the PortPrototypes owned by the SwComponentType.
title: Propagation of mode information

expression: Ports with ModeSwitchInterfaces cannot be connected across ECU boundaries.
title: Local communication of mode switches

expression: A software component is not allowed to type multiple PortPrototypes with ModeSwitchInterfaces where the contained ModeDeclarationGroupPrototypes are referencing ModeDeclarationGroups with identical shortNames but different ModeDeclarations.
title: Different ModeDeclarationGroups shall have different shortNames.

expression: The only allowed values of swCalibrationAccess aggregated by ModeDeclarationGroupPrototype are notAccessible and readOnly.
title: Allowed values of SwCalibrationAccessEnum for ModeDeclarationGroupPrototype

expression: If ModeDeclarationGroupPrototype.swCalibrationAccess is set to readOnly a referenced FlatInstanceDescriptor.swDataDefProps may in turn refer to a CompuMethod that defines the particular literals used in the MCD system for displaying values of the the measured ModeDeclarationGroupPrototypes.
title: Define literals for an MCD system in the context of a FlatInstanceDescriptor

expression: The multiplicity of the aggregation of ModeDeclarationGroupPrototype to ModeSwitchInterface is pragmatically limited to 1.
title: ModeDeclarationGroupPrototype per ModeSwitchInterface

expression: Eventually, a CompositionSwComponentType requires and provides the modes that are required or provided by its contained SwComponentPrototypes. The delegation of these modes from SwComponentPrototypes to the enclosing CompositionSwComponentType is explicitly described by DelegationSwConnectors.
title: CompositionSwComponentType requires and provides the modes that are required or provided by its contained SwComponentPrototypes

expression: The ability to request a mode (i.e. the second use case) is modeled on the VFB via a SenderReceiverInterface and for the RTE it is like a usual communication, that means the connector can also cross ECU boundaries and the communicated dataElements have to be based on AutosarDataTypes.
title: Request mode change

expression: In addition to the formal specification required to implement the communication via ports, a PortPrototype may own so-called port annotations (please find a summary in Figure 4.20). They do not directly influence the signature of calls via this PortPrototype, but contain further information that may be useful for the application developers of the components on both sides of the connection.
title: PortPrototype may own port annotations

expression: Beside formally specified attributes it is also possible to place textual information as provided in GeneralAnnotation.
title: GeneralAnnotation

expression: Typical annotations for sender/receiver communication are: bullet Signal Age: this attribute expresses that the associated software-component will only work correctly given that the propagation of the signal from a sensor to a consumer can be finished within a particular time-limit. Of course, this cannot be identified on component or role level, but has to take into account the instance view as well as the actual ECU- and bus-scheduling. bullet Raw: a raw signal is typically taken directly from the basic software modules of the ECU abstraction layer. In particular, no sensor software-component has filtered its original value. A dataElement in an RPortPrototype of a SwComponentType using this annotation indicates to the control engineer (who develops a control-algorithm for this component) that the signal has to be filtered (This relationship applies for SenderReceiverInterfaces). bullet Filtered: this attribute indicates that a raw signal has been manipulated by some application software-components by using a certain filter. bullet Computed: this attribute indicates that this signal is not measured directly but calculated from tentatively several other measured or calculated signals. In a vehicle, there might be alternative signals to be used from other components having a better quality, e.g. a raw signal. bullet Min: this annotation indicates that the signal carries a minimum value. If, for example, a reference value computed in the software-component is below that value some dedicated actions (e.g. failure-mode) might have to be taken. bullet Max: this annotation indicates that the signal carries a maximum value. If, for example, a reference value computed in the software-component is above that value some dedicated actions (e.g. failure-mode) might have to be taken. In the meta-model this aspect is implemented by the abstract meta-class SenderReceiverAnnotation which represents the base class of both SenderAnnotation and ReceiverAnnotation. This relationship is depicted in Figure 4.21.
title: Typical annotations for sender/receiver communication

expression: The Min and Max annotations are valid for a certain amount of time. The value is likely to change to another valid value while the ECU is running. E.g. the maximal torque which can be requested from an engine is a typical use-case.
title: Min and Max annotations are valid for a certain amount of time

expression: These annotations [Min and Max of SenderReceiverAnnotation] shall not be mismatched with the min and max attributes of CompuMethods.
title: Distinction between SenderReceiverAnnotation Min/Max and CompuMethod Min/Max

expression: The application level port annotations for sender/receiver communication have to be associated to each dataElement in a PortPrototype.
title: Sender/Receiver Annotations Association with DataElement

expression: Furthermore, if two VariableDataPrototypes use the same application-level SenderReceiverAnnotation, a reference from the annotation to the VariableDataPrototypes will be established by an appropriate tool.
title: VariableDataPrototypes use the same application-level SenderReceiverAnnotation

expression: As shown in Figure 4.21 the SenderReceiverAnnotation for sender/receiver communication are grouped into bullet processing type, indicating to some extend the direct quality of the signal, bullet computed, which is just a flag or, bullet limit type, showing the component expects an actual limit. In the case of an RPortPrototype, the signal age of the value, carried by the associated SwConnector, can be specified. Each of these groups can be interpreted as a property of the signal-quality.
title: Grouping for SenderReceiverAnnotation

expression: A SenderReceiverAnnotation shall only be aggregated by a PortPrototype typed by a SenderReceiverInterface.
title: Context of SenderReceiverAnnotation

expression: The ClientServerAnnotation can be used to provide more information with respect to the ClientServerOperation of the PortPrototype.
title: ClientServerAnnotation

expression: A ClientServerAnnotation shall only be aggregated by a PortPrototype typed by a ClientServerInterface.
title: Context of ClientServerAnnotation

expression: IoHwAbstractionServerAnnotation can be used for all kinds of PortInterfaces except NvDataInterface.
title: Usage of IoHwAbstractionServerAnnotation

expression: The ClientServerOperations provide an ArgumentDataPrototype where several annotations can be assigned to. They are depicted in the IoHwAbstraction ServerAnnotation meta-class in Figure 4.23.
title: Assign several annotations to ArgumentDataPrototype

expression: The ParameterPortAnnotation can be used to provide more information with respect to calibration parameter prototypes of the PortPrototype. The data provided at the PortPrototype is calibration parameters. The ParameterPortAnnotation provides a reference to a particular ParameterDataPrototype.
title: ParameterPortAnnotation

expression: A ParameterPortAnnotation shall only be aggregated by a PPortPrototype owned by a ParameterSwComponentType.
title: Context of ParameterPortAnnotation

expression: The ModePortAnnotation can be used to provide more information with respect to the mode declaration group prototype of the PortPrototype.
title: ModePortAnnotation

expression: A ModePortAnnotation shall only be aggregated by a PortPrototype typed by a ModeSwitchInterface.
title: Context of ModePortAnnotation

expression: The TriggerPortAnnotation can be used to provide more information with respect to the trigger of the PortPrototype.
title: TriggerPortAnnotation

expression: A TriggerPortAnnotation shall only be aggregated by a PortPrototype typed by a TriggerInterface.
title: Context of TriggerPortAnnotation

expression: The NvDataPortAnnotation can be used to provide more information with respect to the non volatile data of the PortPrototype.
title: NvDataPortAnnotation

expression: An NvDataPortAnnotation shall only be aggregated by a PortPrototype typed by an NvDataInterface.
title: Context of NvDataPortAnnotation

expression: The DelegatedPortAnnotation is used to define the Signal Fan In or Signal Fan Out inside the CompositionSwComponentType. This information is used to pre-define and pre-check resulting communication patterns in the VFB (1:n, n:1, 1:1) if empty CompositionSwComponentTypes are used as interface definition for sub-systems. The DelegatedPortAnnotation guides either the system designer in connecting the empty CompositionSwComponentType or the sub-system designer in applying communication pattern (1:n, n:1, 1:1) inside of the CompositionSwComponentType.
title: DelegatedPortAnnotation

expression: The attribute values have following definition: bullet single: the internal connections in the CompositionSwComponentType via DelegationSwConnectors and AssemblySwConnectors are defined in a way that each dataElement present in the SenderReceiverInterfaces or operation in the ClientServerInterfaces of the outer PortPrototype is involved in a 1:1 communication pattern only. bullet nfold: The internal connections in the CompositionSwComponentType via DelegationSwConnectors and AssemblySwConnectors are defined in a way that at least one dataElement present in the SenderReceiverInterfaces or one operation in the ClientServerInterfaces of the outer PortPrototype is involved in a 1:n or n:1 communication pattern.
title: Semantics of DelegatedPortAnnotation.signalFan

expression: A DelegatedPortAnnotation shall only be aggregated by a PortPrototype aggregated by a CompositionSwComponentType.
title: Context of DelegatedPortAnnotation

expression: The communication specification is optional, i.e. its existence is not required in any case.
title: ComSpec Optionality
condition_expression: the communication specification is optional, i.e. its existence is not required in any case.

expression: The usage of ComSpecs is not restricted to the PortPrototypes of AtomicSwComponentTypes.
title: ComSpec Usage Scope

expression: Specific subclasses of ComSpec can only be owned by PortPrototypes typed by the corresponding kind of PortInterface.
title: ComSpec Subclass and PortInterface Typing

expression: Within the context of one PPortPrototype there can only be one PPortComSpec that references a given dataElement or clientServerOperation.
title: Limitation on the number of PPortComSpecs in the context of one PPortPrototype

expression: Within the context of one RPortPrototype, there can only be one RPortComSpec that references a given dataElement or clientServerOperation.
title: Limitation on the number of RPortComSpecs in the context of one RPortPrototype

expression: In contrast to PPortPrototype and RPortPrototype, PRPortPrototype can own both RPortComSpecs and PPortComSpecs at the same time.
title: PRPortPrototype can own both RPortComSpecs and PPortComSpecs

expression: Within the context of one PRPortPrototype, there can only be one RPortComSpec and one PPortComSpec that references a given dataElement or clientServerOperation.
title: Limitation on the number of RPortComSpecs/PPortComSpecs in the context of one PRPortPrototype

expression: The allowed combinations of a specific kind of PortInterface and a kind of ComSpec are documented in Table 4.59.
title: PortInterface vs. ComSpec

expression: A SenderReceiverInterface is compatible with SenderComSpec and ReceiverComSpec.
title: SenderReceiverInterface ComSpec Compatibility

expression: A ClientServerInterface is compatible with ClientComSpec and ServerComSpec.
title: ClientServerInterface ComSpec Compatibility

expression: A ModeSwitchInterface is compatible with ModeSwitchSenderComSpec and ModeSwitchReceiverComSpec.
title: ModeSwitchInterface ComSpec Compatibility

expression: A ParameterInterface is compatible with ParameterProvideComSpec and ParameterRequireComSpec.
title: ParameterInterface ComSpec Compatibility

expression: An NvDataInterface is compatible with NvRequireComSpec and NvProvideComSpec.
title: NvDataInterface ComSpec Compatibility

expression: PortPrototypes owned by CompositionSwComponentTypes can have ComSpecs.
title: ComSpecs on PortPrototypes of CompositionSwComponentType

expression: It is not required that the ComSpecs defined on the composition level (on PortPrototypes of CompositionSwComponentType) match the ComSpecs defined inside the constituent AtomicSwComponentTypes.
title: ComSpec Matching Not Required for Compositions

expression: Sender-receiver communication might be queued or non-queued. This aspect is primarily reflected in the value of dataElement.swDataDefProps.swImplPolicy. If the value of this attribute is set to queued then QueuedSenderComSpec and/or QueuedReceiverComSpec shall be defined. In all other applicable cases NonqueuedSenderComSpec resp. NonqueuedReceiverComSpec shall be used. Thus, the constraints [constr_1129], [constr_1130], [constr_1131], and [constr_1132] shall apply. While in the case of queued communication the queueLength attribute remains the only information item the non-queued case foresees several attributes for controlling communication behavior.
title: ComSpec for queued and non-queued sender-receiver communication

expression: A NonqueuedReceiverComSpec that has attribute enableUpdate set to true may not reference a dataElement that in turn is referenced by a VariableAccess in the role dataReadAccess.
title: NonqueuedReceiverComSpec and enableUpdate

expression: The optional attribute initValue shall exist if the enclosing NonqueuedReceiverComSpec is owned by an RPortPrototype.
title: initValue shall exist in an RPortPrototype
condition_expression: the optional attribute initvalue shall exist if the enclosing nonqueuedreceivercomspec is owned by an rportprototype.

expression: The attribute swImplPolicy of a dataElement referenced by a NonqueuedReceiverComSpec shall not be set to the value queued.
title: swImplPolicy and NonqueuedReceiverComSpec

expression: The attribute swImplPolicy of a dataElement referenced by a QueuedReceiverComSpec shall be set to the value queued.
title: swImplPolicy and QueuedReceiverComSpec

expression: The aggregation of VariableAccess in the role ReceiverComSpec.replaceWith shall exist if and only if at least one of the following conditions is fulfilled: bullet Attribute ReceiverComSpec.handleOutOfRange is set to the value externalReplacement. bullet Attribute SenderReceiverInterface.invalidationPolicy.handleInvalid is set to the value externalReplacement.
title: Existence of ReceiverComSpec.replaceWith
condition_expression: the aggregation of variableaccess in the role receivercomspec.replacewith shall exist if and only if at least one of the following conditions is fulfilled: bullet attribute receivercomspec.handleoutofrange is set to the value externalreplacement. bullet attribute senderreceiverinterface.invalidationpolicy.handleinvalid is set to the value externalreplacement.

expression: The attribute swImplPolicy of a dataElement referenced by a NonqueuedSenderComSpec shall not be set to the value queued.
title: swImplPolicy and NonqueuedSenderComSpec

expression: The attribute swImplPolicy of a dataElement referenced by a QueuedSenderComSpec shall be set to the value queued.
title: swImplPolicy and QueuedSenderComSpec

expression: For every RPortPrototype typed by a SenderReceiverInterface a DataFilter can be defined given that non-queued communication is foreseen.
title: DataFilter

expression: This OSEK specification states that "filtering is only used for messages that can be interpreted as C language unsigned integer types (characters, unsigned integers and enumerations)."
title: Applicability of DataFilter

expression: According to the origin of DataFilter, i.e. OSEK COM 3.0.3 specification [18], DataFilters can only be applied to values with an integer base type.
title: Applicability of DataFilter

expression: The attribute ReceiverComSpec.usesEndToEndProtection shall be set to false for all ReceiverComSpec that aggregate EndToEndTransformationDescription in the role transformationComSpecProps.
title: Applicability of attribute ReceiverComSpec.usesEndToEndProtection

expression: The aggregation of networkRepresentation at the ReceiverComSpec or SenderComSpec only applies for dataElements typed by ApplicationPrimitiveDataTypes. For the case of using an ApplicationCompositeDataType an additional mechanism shall be used. In particular, compositeNetworkRepresentation shall be used to define the networkRepresentation of leaf elements of ApplicationCompositeDataTypes.
title: Applicability of networkRepresentation for ApplicationCompositeDataType

expression: If a ReceiverComSpec or SenderComSpec aggregates networkRepresentation it shall not aggregate compositeNetworkRepresentation at the same time (and vice versa).
title: Existence of networkRepresentation vs. compositeNetworkRepresentation

expression: If at least one compositeNetworkRepresentation exists then for each leaf ApplicationCompositeElementDataPrototype of the affected ApplicationCompositeDataType exactly one compositeNetworkRepresentation shall be defined.
title: Existence of compositeNetworkRepresentation shall be comprehensive
condition_expression: if at least one compositenetworkrepresentation exists then for each leaf applicationcompositeelementdataprototype of the affected applicationcompositedatatype exactly one compositenetworkrepresentation shall be defined.

expression: If the attribute enhancedModeApi is defined in a ModeSwitchReceiverComSpec owned by a PRPortPrototype its value shall be ignored.
title: Duplicate existence of enhancedModeApi in the context of a PRPortPrototype

expression: Please note that (along the example of sender-receiver communication) only the initValue defined in the context of a ParameterProvideComSpec or ParameterRequireComSpec is relevant for connections to the corresponding PortPrototype. An initValue defined in the scope of a ParameterDataPrototype is ignored.
title: initValue on the level of a ComSpec is relevant for connections to the corresponding PortPrototype

expression: An AtomicSwComponentType may have AbstractRequiredPortPrototypes typed by an NvDataInterface. If such an AbstractRequiredPortPrototype remains unconnected the nvData still need to have reasonable value.
title: AtomicSwComponentType may have AbstractRequiredPortPrototypes typed by an NvDataInterface

expression: Only the initValue defined in the context of a NvRequireComSpec is relevant for connections to the corresponding PortPrototype. An initValue defined in the scope of a VariableDataPrototype is ignored.
title: NvData initValue relevance

expression: The configuration in EndToEndTransformationComSpecProps is applicable to E2E transformer (protocol of TransformationTechnology is set to EndToEnd). The configuration in UserDefinedTransformationComSpecProps is applicable to a user-defined transformer.
title: Transformer applicability for TransformationComSpecProps subtypes

expression: If more than one user-defined transformer is used within one transformer chain (defined by meta-class TransformationTechnology), the UserDefinedTransformationComSpecProps shall be assigned to the correct user-defined custom transformer in TransformationTechnology.
title: More than one user-defined transformer is used within one transformer chain

expression: A specific DataTransformation shall only be referenced by either bullet a DataPrototypeMapping in the role firstToSecondDataTransformation or bullet an ISignal in the role dataTransformation or bullet an ISignalGroup in the role comBasedSignalGroupTransformation
title: Reference to a specific DataTransformation

expression: A VariableDataPrototype in the context of a PortPrototype shall not be referenced by a DataPrototypeMapping that references a DataTransformation while a DataMapping exists that points to this VariableDataPrototype (via the SystemSignal) that also refers to an ISignal that in turn references a DataTransformation.
title: Restrictions on the relation between DataPrototypeMapping and DataTransformation

expression: This can be done by means of interfacing the BSW in three alternative (as in “one of”) ways: bullet ComM: ClientServerInterface using the standardized ComM_UserRequest.GetCurrentComMode [20] bullet ComM: ModeSwitchInterface using the standardized ComM_CurrentMode.currentMode [20] bullet BswM: ModeSwitchInterface using the standardized AppModeInterface.currentMode [15]
title: BSW Interfacing Alternatives for Partial Networking

expression: the ComM can be retrieved by either a ClientServerInterface or a SenderReceiverInterface. Which of the two alternatives applies in a specific case is up to the author of a software-component.
title: Choice of ComM Retrieval Method for Software Component Author

expression: To assure that the communication via PortPrototypes that belong to a partial network is valid the software component shall consider the status of the partial network before communicating in order to assert its activity.
title: Partial Network Status Check Before Communication

expression: A status port shall not become a member of the PortGroup that corresponds to the partial network subject to the status port. The relationship is implemented by means of a specific SwcServiceDependency that owns a RoleBasedPortAssignment to the intended status port.
title: Status port shall not become a member of the PortGroup

expression: The information (in terms of ConsistencyNeeds) can be defined primarily during the design of an AtomicSwComponentType but it is just as well possible to specify this ConsistencyNeeds during the definition of CompositionSwComponentTypes.
title: Context for Defining ConsistencyNeeds in Component Types

expression: In order to be able to clearly separate the aspect of stability from coherence it is possible to use the roles dpgDoesNotRequireCoherence to express that a group of VariableDataPrototypes explicitly does not require consistency. Likewise, regDoesNotRequireStability can be used to express that for a group of RunnableEntitys stability with respect to data access is not required.
title: Stability and/or coherence is not required

expression: ConsistencyNeeds can only be applied to RunnableEntitys that make use of "implicit" communication.
title: Applicability of ConsistencyNeeds

expression: If a ConsistencyNeeds is applied on RunnableEntitys that do not use implicit communication it shall be ignored.
title: ConsistencyNeeds applied on RunnableEntitys that do not use implicit communication

expression: If ConsistencyNeeds are aggregated by a CompositionSwComponentType the associations stereotyped (cid:28)instanceRef(cid:29) may only refer to context and target elements within the context of this CompositionSwComponentType.
title: ConsistencyNeeds aggregated by CompositionSwComponentType

expression: If ConsistencyNeeds are aggregated by a AtomicSwComponentType the associations stereotyped (cid:28)instanceRef(cid:29) may only refer to context and target elements within the context of this AtomicSwComponentType.
title: ConsistencyNeeds aggregated by AtomicSwComponentType

expression: If a receiving SwComponentType owns a DataPrototypeGroup in the role dpgRequiresCoherence for one or several of its RunnableEntitys it is required that VariableDataPrototypes belonging to the same DataPrototypeGroup are produced coherently. This means the values of the VariableDataPrototypes shall be of the same age.
title: Receiving SwComponentType owns a DataPrototypeGroup in the role dpgRequiresCoherence

expression: If a receiving SwComponentType owns a RunnableEntityGroup in the role regRequiresStability for one or several of its RunnableEntitys it is required that the values of implicitly communicated VariableDataPrototypes are kept stable over the execution of all RunnableEntitys belonging to the given RunnableEntityGroup.
title: Receiving SwComponentType owns a RunnableEntityGroup in the role regRequiresStability

expression: If a receiving SwComponentType owns a RunnableEntityGroup in the role regRequiresStability and also owns one or several DataPrototypeGroups in the role dpgRequiresCoherence it is required that values of VariableDataPrototypes belonging to the same DataPrototypeGroup are produced coherently. This means that the values of the VariableDataPrototypes shall be of the same age and are kept stable over the execution of all RunnableEntitys belonging to the given RunnableEntityGroup.
title: Receiving SwComponentType owns a RunnableEntityGroup in the role regRequiresStability and also owns one or several DataPrototypeGroups in the role dpgRequiresCoherence

expression: If a sending SwComponentType owns a DataPrototypeGroup in the role dpgRequiresCoherence for one or several of its RunnableEntitys it is required that VariableDataPrototypes belonging to the same DataPrototypeGroup are propagated at the same point of time to RunnableEntitys which are not belonging to the group of producing RunnableEntitys (which may, but don’t have to be formally described as a RunnableEntity Group).
title: Sending SwComponentType owns a DataPrototypeGroup in the role dpgRequiresCoherence

expression: If a sending SwComponentType owns a DataPrototypeGroup in the role dpgRequiresCoherence, RunnableEntityGroups in the role regDoesNotRequireStability may exist. Read accesses from RunnableEntitys in those RunnableEntityGroups will not read the coherent values but the intermediary values written by RunnableEntitys of the same group.
title: Sending SwComponentType owns a DataPrototypeGroup in the role dpgRequiresCoherence and also RunnableEntityGroups

expression: For the case of sender and receiver of the same implicitly communicated VariableDataPrototypes are associated with the same RunnableEntityGroup [TPS_SWCT_01472], [TPS_SWCT_01473], [TPS_SWCT_01475] as well as [TPS_SWCT_01475] apply with the exception that updates of the values of implicitly communicated VariableDataPrototypes inside the given RunnableEntityGroup become visible immediately after the producing RunnableEntity was terminated.
title: Sender and receiver of the same implicitly communicated VariableDataPrototypes are associated with the same RunnableEntity Group

expression: Within one DataTypeMappingSet, a ModeDeclarationGroup shall not be mapped to different ImplementationDataTypes.
title: Unambiguous mapping of modes to data types

expression: For every ModeDeclarationGroup referenced by a ModeDeclarationGroupPrototype used in a PortPrototype typed by a ModeSwitchInterface a ModeRequestTypeMap shall exist that points to the ModeDeclarationGroup and also to an eligible ImplementationDataType. The ModeRequestTypeMap shall be aggregated by a DataTypeMappingSet which is referenced from the SwcInternalBehavior that is owned by the ApplicationSwComponentType that also owns the PortPrototype.
title: Restrictions of ModeRequestTypeMap

expression: PortPrototypes typed by a ParameterInterface can either be PPortPrototypes or RPortPrototypes. The usage of PRPortPrototypes that are typed by a ParameterInterface is not supported.
title: PortPrototypes typed by a ParameterInterface

expression: The mapping is described separately from the SwConnector as reusable ARElement. A set of PortInterfaceMappings is grouped in a PortInterfaceMappingSet.
title: Mapping is described separately from the SwConnector as reusable ARElement

expression: The existence of a PortInterfaceMapping overrides all other compatibility rules given that the following statements are fulfilled: bullet [constr_1071] applies also for the application of a PortInterfaceMapping. bullet [constr_1268] applies also for the application of a PortInterfaceMapping. bullet [constr_1269] applies also for the application of a PortInterfaceMapping. bullet [constr_1270] applies also for the application of a PortInterfaceMapping. bullet A structural difference between mapped DataPrototypes can be mitigated by means of a SubElementMapping. This includes the case that a “structure” data type is mapped to an “array” data type and vice versa. [TPS_SWCT_01195] is also applicable. When using a PortInterfaceMapping, the developer of a software-component needs to properly understand the consequences in terms of model semantics.
title: PortInterfaceMapping overrides all other compatibility rules

expression: Each PortInterfaceMapping describes the mapping of the PortInterface elements of exactly two PortInterfaces.
title: PortInterfaceMapping

expression: To apply a PortInterfaceMapping, a SwConnector has to reference that PortInterfaceMapping.
title: SwConnector Reference to PortInterfaceMapping

expression: A PortInterfaceMapping is only applicable and valid for a SwConnector if the two PortPrototypes which are referenced by the SwConnector are typed by the same two PortInterfaces which are mapped by the PortInterfaceMapping.
title: Applicability of PortInterfaceMapping

expression: The mapping via PortInterfaceMapping has a higher precedence than the mapping by equal shortNames as defined in chapter 6. If a connector has an associated PortInterfaceMapping this mapping shall be strictly binding with respect to the number of mapped data elements.
title: Precedence of PortInterfaceMapping

expression: Unmapped PortInterface elements will not be connected by the referencing SwConnector.
title: Unmapped elements of PortInterfaces

expression: Within one VariableAndParameterInterfaceMapping all firstDataPrototypes shall belong to one and only one DataInterface and all secondDataPrototypes shall belong to one other and only one other DataInterface.
title: Consistency of VariableAndParameterInterfaceMapping with respect to the referenced DataInterfaces

expression: Nevertheless, the possible mappings of VariableDataPrototypes and ParameterDataPrototypes are restricted by the swImplPolicy attribute.
title: Possible mappings are restricted by the swImplPolicy

expression: It is not possible to define a mapping between an element where the swImplPolicy is set to queued and an other element where the swImplPolicy is set differently.
title: Relevance of swImplPolicy

expression: The conversion of elements of SenderReceiverInterfaces is possible if one of the following conditions applies: bullet The AutosarDataTypes of the referred DataPrototypes are compatible as described in chapter 6.2. bullet A conversion of the data as described in chapter 4.3.2 is available. bullet A DataPrototypeMapping.firstToSecondDataTransformation is defined.
title: Conversion of SenderReceiverInterfaces

expression: Either the AutosarDataTypes of the referred ArgumentDataPrototypes are compatible as described in chapter 6.2 or a conversion of the data as described in chapter 4.3.2 is available.
title: Conversion of ClientServerInterfaces

expression: All ClientServerOperations referenced by a ClientServerOperationMapping in the role firstOperation shall belong to exactly one ClientServerInterface. All ClientServerOperations referenced by a ClientServerOperationMapping in the role secondOperation shall belong to exactly one other ClientServerInterface.
title: Scope of mapped ClientServerOperations in the context of a ClientServerOperationMapping

expression: All ApplicationErrors referenced by a ClientServerApplicationErrorMapping in the role firstApplicationError shall belong to exactly one ClientServerInterface. All ApplicationErrors referenced by a ClientServerApplicationErrorMapping in the role secondApplicationError shall belong to exactly one other ClientServerInterface.
title: Scope of mapped ApplicationErrors in the context of a ClientServerOperationMapping

expression: For each argument owned by a ClientServerOperationMapping.firstOperation and ClientServerOperationMapping.secondOperation a reference in the role ClientServerOperationMapping.argumentMapping.firstDataPrototype or ClientServerOperationMapping.argumentMapping.secondDataPrototype shall exist originated by one of the ClientServerOperationMapping.argumentMappings owned by the mentioned ClientServerOperationMapping.
title: Consistency of ArgumentDataPrototypes within the context of a ClientServerOperationMapping

expression: Within the context of a ClientServerOperationMapping, the value of the argument ArgumentDataPrototype.direction of two mapped ArgumentDataPrototype shall be identical.
title: ArgumentDataPrototype.direction shall be preserved in a ClientServerOperationMapping

expression: Within the context of a ClientServerOperationMapping, the number of arguments of firstOperation and secondOperation shall be identical.
title: Number of arguments shall be preserved in a ClientServerOperationMapping

expression: Within the context of a ClientServerOperationMapping, each argument shall only be referenced once in the role firstDataPrototype or secondDataPrototype.
title: ArgumentDataPrototype shall be mapped only once in a ClientServerOperationMapping

expression: The mapping of ModeDeclarationGroupPrototypes is only valid if these are typed by (read "refer to") compatible ModeDeclarationGroups according chapter 6.7.
title: Validity of ModeInterfaceMapping

expression: Within the scope of one ModeDeclarationMappingSet, all firstModes shall belong to one and only one ModeDeclarationGroup and all secondModes shall belong to one and only one other ModeDeclarationGroup
title: Consistency of firstMode and secondMode in the scope of one ModeDeclarationMappingSet

expression: If a ModeDeclarationGroupPrototypeMapping.modeDeclarationMappingSet exists, the ModeDeclarationGroup owning the modeDeclarations referenced in the role firstMode shall be the type of the ModeDeclarationGroupPrototypeMapping.firstModeGroup and the ModeDeclarationGroup owning the modeDeclarations referenced in the role secondMode shall be the type of the ModeDeclarationGroupPrototypeMapping.secondModeGroup.
title: Consistency of ModeDeclarationMappingSet with respect to the referenced firstModeGroup and secondModeGroup

expression: The mode that corresponds to the ModeDeclaration of the Mode User is entered or exited when the mode of the mode manager that corresponds to the mapped (i.e. referenced by the same ModeDeclarationMapping) ModeDeclaration of the mode manager is entered or exited.
title: ModeDeclaration of a mode user is mapped to exactly one ModeDeclaration of a mode manager

expression: The mode that corresponds to the mapped ModeDeclaration of the mode user is entered when any of the modes of the Mode Manager that correspond to ModeDeclarations referenced by the applicable ModeDeclarationMapping is entered. The mode that corresponds to the mapped ModeDeclaration of the mode user is exited when any of the modes of the Mode Manager that correspond to ModeDeclarations referenced by the applicable ModeDeclarationMapping is exited if the new mode is not mapped to related mode of the mode user.
title: ModeDeclaration of a mode user is mapped to several ModeDeclarations of a mode manager

expression: If one ModeDeclaration of a mode user is mapped to several ModeDeclarations of a mode manager by means of several ModeDeclarationMappings, the intended semantics is that individual mode transitions of the mode manager represent 'exit' and 'enter' events for the Mode User, and these transitions are recognizable by the mode user.
title: Semantics of Mode User Mapped to Multiple Mode Manager Declarations via Multiple Mappings

expression: If one ModeDeclaration of a mode user is mapped to several ModeDeclarations of a mode manager in the context of a single ModeDeclarationMapping (utilizing multiplicity of the role firstMode), the semantics is that individual mode transitions of the Mode Manager are not recognizable to the Mode User.
title: Semantics of Mode User Mapped to Multiple Mode Manager Declarations via Single Mapping (firstMode multiplicity)

expression: A configuration that maps several ModeDeclarations representing modes of a mode user to one ModeDeclaration representing a mode of a mode manager shall be rejected.
title: Mapping of ModeDeclarations of mode user to ModeDeclaration of mode manager

expression: On the level of the Software Component Template, partial networking is supported by means of the concept of a “Virtual Function Cluster” (VFC). The latter groups all communication on the VFB with respect to a given function. However, the conceptual idea of a Virtual Function Cluster is not represented in the meta-model as such. Instead, PortGroups (see chapter 4.6) are used to specify the grouping of PortPrototypes to the higher conceptual level of a Virtual Function Cluster.
title: Support for partial networking

expression: The purpose of Virtual Function Cluster within the Software Component Template mainly has three aspects: 1. assign PortPrototypes (non service related) of Sender Receiver or Client Server communication to Virtual Function Clusters. 2. control the behavior of the corresponding function in terms of whether or not it is required at a given point in time. This aspect is implemented by the concept of a control port. Software-components that implement control ports of a Virtual Function Cluster conceptually become VFC Controllers. 3. allow for the application software to retrieve the status of a given Virtual Function Cluster. This aspect is implemented by the concept of a status port.
title: Purpose of Virtual Function Cluster

expression: The usage of the generic concept of PortGroups for the purpose of partial networks shall be indicated by setting the value of the attribute category of PortGroup to PARTIAL_NETWORKING.
title: PortGroup Category for Partial Networking

expression: The purpose of a control port is to request or release a VFC. Requesting means that the VFC is actively using the communication resources while release boils down to the VFC being inactive, i.e. corresponding partial network may be shut down until further notice. As the requesting and releasing semantics is implemented by means of interfacing the BSW the corresponding control ports need to be typed by a PortInterface that has the attribute isService set to true.
title: Purpose of a control port

expression: For requesting and releasing partial networks, the BSW can be interfaced in two alternative (i.e. either one or the other) ways: bullet ComM: ClientServerInterface using the standardized ComM_UserRequest.RequestComMode [20] bullet BswM: SenderReceiverInterface using the standardized AppModeRequestInterface.requestedMode [15]
title: Requesting and releasing partial networks

expression: Please note that the control port shall not become a part of the PortGroup that defines the particular VFC the control port is going to service. The relationship is implemented by means of a specific SwcServiceDependency that owns a RoleBasedPortAssignment to the intended control port.
title: Control port shall not become a part of the PortGroup

expression: Very much like mode management, the concept of partial networking supports the ability to actively query the status of a partial network.
title: Actively query the status of a partial network
